record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: Fix n. As d tends to infinity, what is the smallest possible dimension Δ of an irreducible component of the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^n, 0)? Equivalently, what can be said asymptotically about (nd - Δ) / d?

evidence.quote: Problem XXII. Fix n. What is the smallest dimension Δ of a component of Hilbd(A^n, 0), when d → ∞? Or, a bit more precisely, what can be said asymptotically about 1/d · (nd − Δ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ be a fixed integer and let $\mathbb{A}^n$ denote affine $n$-space over an algebraically closed field. For a positive integer $d$, let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n, 0)$ denote the punctual Hilbert scheme parametrizing zero-dimensional closed subschemes of $\mathbb{A}^n$ of length $d$ that are supported at the origin $0 \in \mathbb{A}^n$. Let
$$\Delta(n,d) := \min\{\dim Z : Z \text{ is an irreducible component of } \mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n, 0)\}.$$
Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\Delta(n,d)$ as $d \to \infty$ (with $n$ fixed). More precisely, determine
$$\liminf_{d\to\infty} \frac{nd - \Delta(n,d)}{d} \quad \text{and} \quad \limsup_{d\to\infty} \frac{nd - \Delta(n,d)}{d},$$
or any sharp asymptotic estimate for $(nd - \Delta(n,d))/d$.
artifact.status_search_result: The minimum dimension of irreducible components of the punctual Hilbert scheme remains an active area of research. While all smoothable components are known to have dimension at least (n-1)(d-1) (with curvilinear components achieving this bound), the question of the smallest possible component dimension across all (including elementary/non-smoothable) components for fixed n as d → ∞ has not been resolved. Recent work has constructed small elementary components for n ≥ 4, but no sharp asymptotic formula for Δ(n,d) appears to be established.
